# dotnet-test-solution-nested

The **solution-rooted** .NET layout: a `*.sln` at the root and every
project at **depth 2** under `src/` and `tests/`. This is what
`dotnet new sln` + `dotnet sln add` conventions produce, and it is the
layout the `dotnet-expensable` evaluation seed uses.

## Why this fixture exists

`dotnet_adapter._detect_test_project` used to glob `*.csproj` and
`*/*.csproj` only. Against this layout it found **nothing**: `novetest
init` at the solution root reported `state: "engine-misconfigured"` and
`novetest test` exited 4 — on a solution that `dotnet test` runs
perfectly. Discovery now also reads the `*.sln`, which was already the
marker that made the workspace .NET in the first place. Filed as
`agent-comms/questions/run-team-2026-08-04-p7-dotnet-localization-reachability.md`;
exercised by `tests/integration/run/test_dotnet_solution_nested.py`.

`dotnet-test-basic/` keeps covering the flat depth-1 layout. The two
fixtures share their test contract byte-for-byte so that any difference
between their Run Records is attributable to discovery alone.

## Layout

```
dotnet-test-solution-nested/
├── nested.sln                          # authored by `dotnet sln add`, not by hand
├── src/MathLib/MathLib.csproj          # library under test        (depth 2)
├── tests/MathLib.Tests/…csproj         # xUnit test project        (depth 2)
└── samples/TestBed/TestBed.csproj      # THE DECOY — see below     (depth 2)
```

The solution file is **UTF-8 with a BOM, CRLF-terminated, and
backslash-separated** — as every real `.sln` is, on every OS. It also
carries three *solution folder* entries (`src`, `tests`, `samples`)
which use the project line's exact syntax with a label in the path
slot. A parser that assumes any of that away passes on a hand-written
`.sln` and fails on a real one, so this file was generated by the
`dotnet` CLI rather than typed.

## The decoy

`samples/TestBed/TestBed.csproj` is a plain library whose **name carries
the `test` token** and whose path **sorts before `tests/`**. Widening
discovery without a discriminator makes it the winner, which would point
`dotnet test` at a project with no test framework. It is dropped because
it does not declare `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` / `<IsTestProject>`. Do not
"clean it up" — the integration test asserts against it.

## Test contract

| Test | Outcome | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `TestAddPasses` | Passed | Baseline parity with `dotnet-test-basic` |
| `TestSubtractIntentionallyFails` | Failed | `Assert.Equal(5, Subtract(10, 4))` — `Subtract` returns `6`. Do NOT "fix" the assertion. |
| `TestParametrized(a: 1, b: 2, expected: 3)` | Passed | `[Theory]` + `[InlineData]`, for TRX display-name parity |

`dotnet test` exit code on this fixture: **1** (some user tests failed);
`novetest test` exit code: **3**.

## Floor versions (matrix-pinned)

- `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` 17.8.0
- `xunit` 2.6.0 — do NOT downgrade to the 2.5.3 template default
- `xunit.runner.visualstudio` 2.5.3
